'''Michael Glanzberg''' is an American analytic philosopher specializing in [[philosophy of language]] and [[philosophical logic]] who is currently a professor in philosophy at [[Rutgers University]].<ref name="Rutgers">{{cite web |title=Glanzberg, Michael |url=https://philosophy.rutgers.edu/people/faculty/details/182-faculty1/faculty-profiles/1172-blank-faculty-profile-3 |website=Rutgers Department of Philosophy |accessdate=13 September 2020}}</ref> He received his PhD in philosophy from [[Harvard University]], where [[Charles Parsons (philosopher)|Charles Parsons]] and [[Warren Goldfarb]] supervised his dissertation.<ref>{{cite web |title=Michael Glanzberg |url=https://www.genealogy.math.ndsu.nodak.edu/id.php?id=204880 |website=Mathematics Genealogy Project |publisher=Department of Mathematics, North Dakota State University |accessdate=13 September 2020}}</ref> Glanzberg has previously held faculty positions at [[Northwestern University]], [[University of California, Davis]], [[University of Toronto Mississauga|Erindale College]] at the [[University of Toronto]], and [[MIT]].<ref name="Rutgers" /><ref>{{cite web |last1=Webb |first1=Margaret |title=A Tale of Two Campuses |url=https://magazine.utoronto.ca/campus/u-of-t-downtown-vs-suburban-campuses-tri-campus-system/ |publisher=University of Toronto Magazine |date=December 18, 2003}}</ref> Often working at the intersection of logic and the philosophy of language, Glanzberg is recognized for his work on quantification, paradox, semantics, theories of [[truth]], and the role of context in various linguistic settings. He frequently collaborates with [[Jc Beall]].<ref>{{cite book |last1=Beall |first1=JC |last2=Glanzberg |first2=Michael |editor1-last=French |editor1-first=P. A. |editor2-last=Wettstein |editor2-first=H. K. |title=Truth and its Deformities |date=2008 |publisher=Blackwell |chapter=Where the Paths Meet: Remarks on Truth and Paradox}}</ref><ref>{{cite book |last1=Beall |first1=JC |last2=Glanzberg |first2=Michael |last3=Ripley |first3=David |title=Formal Theories of Truth |date=2018 |publisher=Oxford University Press |location=Oxford |pages=160}}</ref><ref name="SEP Liar Paradox">{{cite web |last1=Beall |first1=JC |last2=Glanzberg |first2=Michael |last3=Ripley |first3=David |title=Liar Paradox |url=https://plato.stanford.edu/entries/liar-paradox/ |website=Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy |accessdate=13 September 2020}}</ref> He serves as Co-Editor-in-Chief for the journal [[Linguistics and Philosophy]] and edited The Oxford Handbook of Truth (2018).<ref>Glanzberg, Michael (ed.) (2018). ''The Oxford Handbook of Truth''. Oxford, United Kingdom: Oxford University Press. ISBN 978-0199557929.</ref>
